TEXT.TEXTVALUE: Take a small quantity of ferrous sulphate crystals (FeSO[sub]4[/sub].7H[sub]2[/sub]O) in a dry boiling tube.
Hold the boiling tube with a test tube holder.
Heat the boiling tube over the flame of a burner.
On heating ferrous sulphate crystals, they lose their water molecules and form white coloured crystals of anhydrous ferrous sulphate (FeSO[sub]4[/sub]).

On further heating, anhydrous ferrous sulphate decomposes to form dark brown coloured ferric oxide (Fe[sub]2[/sub]O[sub]3[/sub]), sulphur dioxide (SO[sub]2[/sub]) and sulphur trioxide (SO[sub]3[/sub]) gases. The gas emitted has the odour of burning sulphur.

In this reaction a single reactant FeSO[sub]4[/sub] decomposes to form three different products Fe[sub]2[/sub]O[sub]3[/sub](s), SO[sub]2[/sub](g) and SO[sub]3[/sub](g). So the reaction is a decomposition reaction.
